title: Introduction to Psychology
definitions: The scientific study of behavior and mental processes
The view that all knowledge and thoughts come from experience
The 19th-century school of psychology that argued that breaking down experience into its elemental parts offers the best way to understand thought and behavior
The 19th-century school of psychology that argued it was better to look at why the mind works the way it does than to describe its parts
A school of psychology that proposed that psychology can be a true science only if it examines observable behavior, not ideas, thoughts, feelings, or motives

title: Research Methods
definitions: A systematic approach to gathering information that relies on empirical observation and measurement
A specific, informed, and testable prediction of what kind of outcome should occur under a particular condition
Any factor that can change or vary
A group of participants in an experiment who do not receive the treatment or intervention being tested
A statistical relationship between two variables

title: Social Psychology
definitions: The tendency for people to perform better on simple tasks when in the presence of others
The tendency for people to exert less effort when working in a group
Changing one's behavior to match the responses of others
Following direct commands from an authority figure
The phenomenon where individuals are less likely to take action or feel responsibility in the presence of others

title: Biological Psychology
definitions: A specialized cell that transmits nerve impulses
The junction between two neurons where information is transmitted
A chemical messenger that transmits signals across a synapse
The brain and spinal cord
The nerves and ganglia outside of the brain and spinal cord

title: Sensation and Perception
definitions: The process of detecting physical energy from the environment and encoding it as neural signals
The process of organizing and interpreting sensory information to give it meaning
The minimum amount of stimulation needed to detect a stimulus 50% of the time
The minimum difference between two stimuli that can be detected 50% of the time
A set of principles that describe how we organize and group visual elements

title: Learning
definitions: A type of learning in which a neutral stimulus comes to elicit a response after being paired with a stimulus that naturally elicits that response
A type of learning in which behavior is strengthened if followed by reinforcement or diminished if followed by punishment
A consequence that increases the likelihood that a behavior will occur
A consequence that decreases the likelihood that a behavior will occur
Learning by watching others

title: Memory
definitions: The process of transforming information into a form that can be stored in memory
The process of maintaining information in memory over time
The process of accessing stored information
A limited-capacity store that can hold information for approximately 20 to 30 seconds
A relatively permanent store that can hold vast amounts of information for long periods of time
